blocks.text: [F] OCCL Ltd makes two products: insoluble sulphur, sold under the Diamond Sulf brand as a vulcanising agent mainly to tyre makers, and sulphuric acid and oleum, a co-product sold into the domestic industrial market (PPT Feb 2026; AR2026 p.5). [F] Installed capacity is 39,500 MTPA of insoluble sulphur across Dharuhera, Haryana (17,500 MTPA, 3 lines) and the Mundra SEZ, Gujarat (22,000 MTPA, 4 lines), plus 88,000 MTPA of sulphuric acid/oleum at Dharuhera (PPT Feb 2026). [F] The annual report describes acid capacity as 290 MTPD instead (AR2026 p.5). [MC] Management says insoluble sulphur is about 0.7-0.8% of a tyre's cost and is used at 3-5 parts per hundred rubber (CALL Aug 2025).

[F] It makes money by converting purchased sulphur, mostly refinery by-product, plus coating oil into insoluble sulphur grades that tyre plants have qualified. It also sells sulphuric acid priced on a 'sulphur-plus' basis (CALL Aug 2025; PPT Feb 2026). [F] In FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 505.9 cr: insoluble sulphur Rs 345.0 cr (68%), of which Rs 162.2 cr domestic and Rs 182.8 cr export; sulphuric acid and oleum Rs 160.2 cr (32%), all domestic (AR2026 p.70; AR2026 p.11). [F] Exports were 36% of total revenue and about 53% of insoluble sulphur revenue (AR2026 p.70). [F] Two customers each made up more than 10% of revenue in FY26 and FY25; neither is named (AR2026 p.77). [MC] Management claims 40+ customers in 21 countries, a domestic share of 55-60% and a global share of about 10% (PPT Feb 2026).

blocks.text: [AI] How we classify each driver: (1) trade remedies are company-specific and policy-dependent; (2) spare capacity is company-specific; (3) the Q1 FY27 step-up is cyclical until its drivers are disclosed; (4) acid economics are cyclical; (5) the balance sheet is company-specific; (6) US tariffs are cyclical/policy; (7) qualification barriers are structural.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. [F] Profit did not turn into cash in FY26. Operating cash flow was Rs 11 cr against PAT of Rs 48 cr (CFO/PAT 0.23), and free cash flow was negative at Rs -4 cr (NUMBERS). [F] Inventories rose from Rs 59.9 cr to Rs 94.4 cr, receivables from Rs 64.9 cr to Rs 84.7 cr, and supplier advances from Rs 2.4 cr to Rs 19.7 cr (AR2026 p.55; AR2026 p.67).

2. [F] Reported FY26 PAT includes a one-off Rs 7.04 cr deferred-tax credit from moving to the new tax regime (AR2026 p.70; AR2026 p.73). [E] Excluding it, PAT would have been about Rs 40.7 cr, with an effective tax rate of about 27% rather than 14%.

3. [MC] The anti-dumping duty did not raise margins: Chinese exporters 'absorbed' it and Malaysian imports set the benchmark (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Feb 2026; AR2026 p.10). [AI] Trade remedies have so far defended margins rather than expanded them.

4. [MC] The industry is oversupplied. Global capacity is about 3.57 lakh t (figure put by an analyst, not disputed) against demand of 2.75-3.0 lakh t; global utilisation is 70-75%; demand grows 2-3% a year, implying 'maybe 4-5 years' to a healthy 85% (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Feb 2026).

5. [F] This is a single molecule sold into one end-industry, with two customers each above 10% of revenue (AR2026 p.77; AR2026 p.24). [F] The company itself lists 'limited product diversification' as a weakness (AR2026 p.24).

6. [F] The gross margin proxy fell from about 62% in FY25 (9M) to about 51% in FY26, as acid mix rose from 19% to 32% and sulphur went from Rs 29/kg to Rs 52/kg (AR2026 p.55; AR2026 p.11). [E] Gross margin figures are our computation.

7. [F] Our DCF model returns negative per-share values in the bear (Rs -19.9) and base (Rs -3.9) cases and Rs 7.7 in the bull case, against a price of Rs 219. The reverse DCF finds no growth rate that reconciles with the market value (NUMBERS). [AI] The model has mechanical weaknesses (see the verdict part), but no scenario in it supports the price.

8. [F] Disclosure is thin. Management declined to give volumes, realisations, per-tonne margins, US revenue share or gross margins, citing competition (CALL Jun 2025; CALL Aug 2025; CALL Nov 2025; CALL Feb 2026). [F] Its own documents give export shares of 36%, 37%, 53%, ~55% and 'major turnover' (AR2026 p.5; AR2026 p.39; AR2026 p.25; PPT Feb 2026; AR2026 p.58).

9. [F] Executive pay is high relative to profit. KMP remuneration was about Rs 7.7 cr, or about 16% of FY26 PAT [E]. The MD's pay rose 25% and the JMD's 18%, against a 6% rise in median employee pay (AR2026 p.40; AR2026 p.76).

10. [F] Title deeds for land (Rs 1.6 cr) and buildings (Rs 60.3 cr gross) are still in the demerged company's name nearly two years after the appointed date. The accounting software's audit trail was not enabled at database level (AR2026 p.52; AR2026 p.38).

Is Q1 FY27 a new base or a spike? [F] OPM of 28% in Q1 FY27 compares with 16-21% in each of the previous eight quarters (NUMBERS). [MC] The board points to higher import prices, raw-material security buying by customers and a tight acid market (AR2026 p.33). [AI] The market may be extrapolating a quarter that coincided with a sulphur and acid supply shock. Equally, if the Hormuz-related shortage persists, the cost-plus acid business and better domestic pricing could hold above the old 16-18% band.

Does the trade-remedy stack finally bite? [F] The duty-absorption findings and the CVD initiation are new since the last call (ANNOUNCEMENTS). [AI] The bear case leans on the 2025 experience of absorption. The bull case is that an absorption finding directly targets that behaviour. Neither the final duty quantum nor its notification date is disclosed.

Is the working-capital build deliberate stock-building or a quality problem? [MC] Management says it chose to hold more sulphur and offer longer credit to tyre majors as domestic share rose (CALL Nov 2025; AR2026 p.25). [F] Receivables over six months past due are small, at Rs 5.7 cr (AR2026 p.66). [AI] The build looks policy-driven, but it consumed most of FY26's operating cash.

What is the real moat? [MC] A 24-month qualification period and IATF certification (PPT Feb 2026; AR2026 p.5). [MC] Yet Chinese suppliers did qualify and their 'quality is now acceptable' (CALL Jun 2025; CALL Aug 2025). [AI] The barrier protects incumbency in volume but has not protected price.

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative appears to be 'a protected Indian monopoly-like supplier entering an upcycle'. That narrative is consistent with the stock trading near its 52-week high of Rs 223 against a low of Rs 75 (NUMBERS). Our read differs in two ways. First, OCCL's FY26 earnings were acid-led, tax-assisted and cash-negative after working capital. The trade remedies that were supposed to lift insoluble sulphur margins were offset by input costs. Second, the evidence that OCCL is the 'sole Indian manufacturer' with an ICRA-verified 55-60% domestic share cannot be confirmed from our documents. The rating rationale available to us is a login page (RATING). The 55-60% and ~10% figures appear in the company's own presentation (PPT Feb 2026), which contradicts our earlier dashboard notes that attributed them to ICRA (BOARD). On the other side, the market may underestimate how much operating leverage 30% idle capacity provides if the anti-absorption ruling is notified. The variant view is that this is a cyclical spread business with a policy option, not a compounding franchise.

blocks.text: [AI] The operating business is old: insoluble sulphur since 1994 and acid since 1978. The legal entity and its reporting history are new, with listing in October 2024 and first full year in FY26. Capacity growth stopped in 2021-22. The last insoluble sulphur addition was the 5,500 MTPA Dharuhera line commissioned December 2021 (PPT Feb 2026). [F] Gross block is Rs 628 cr against net block of Rs 355 cr, so about 44% has already been depreciated (AR2026 p.64). [AI] Investors are buying an existing, partly depreciated asset base whose returns depend on spread and utilisation, not a newly built growth platform.

items: 1. Sulphur procurement: [MC] sulphur comes 'easily from oil refineries'; coating oil is bought domestically and internationally (PPT Feb 2026). [MC] Supply was disrupted when Nayara Energy could not supply, and advances had to be paid to secure material (CALL Nov 2025).

2. Sulphuric acid: [F] sulphur is burned at Dharuhera into sulphuric acid and oleum; waste-heat steam from the acid plant meets all the steam needs of the Dharuhera insoluble sulphur plants and drives a turbine (AR2026 p.39; AR2026 p.35).

3. Insoluble sulphur conversion: [MC] OCCL uses an in-house 'low temperature' technology needing less energy than some Chinese high-temperature routes (CALL Aug 2025). It runs several smaller lines that can be switched between grades (CALL Aug 2025).
4. Grading and coating: [F] high-dispersion, high-stability and special grades are offered (PPT Feb 2026).
5. Customer qualification: [MC] at least 24 months for a tyre maker to approve a new supplier (PPT Feb 2026).

6. Sales and logistics: [F] direct sales to tyre makers; an agent and warehouse network abroad; acid sold to institutional and trade buyers (AR2026 p.5; CALL Nov 2025). [F] Freight was 5.9% of FY26 revenue, against about 9% in FY25 per management (AR2026 p.72; CALL Jun 2025) [E].

blocks.text: [AI] Viewed one way, concentration is stable: two customers above 10% in both years, plus a claimed 40+ customer base. Viewed the other way, the push for domestic share is moving volume towards a handful of Indian tyre majors that pay on longer terms. [MC] Management confirms domestic debtor days rose by 4-5 days because tyre majors take longer to pay than the spot market (CALL Nov 2025). [F] Domestic receivables nearly doubled to Rs 59.6 cr (AR2026 p.77). [AI] We read the direction as worsening, with low confidence, because the data needed to test it is not disclosed.

blocks.text: [F] At Rs 219 the share price sits far above all three fair values in our DCF model: bear Rs -19.9, base Rs -3.9, bull Rs 7.7 (NUMBERS). [AI] The gap comes from three things. The model's capital-intensity and margin inputs are conservative relative to current conditions. The market is extrapolating one exceptional quarter. And investors are capitalising a trade-remedy option whose last iteration delivered no margin gain. Our evidence supports a well-financed, cyclical spread business with a policy kicker. It does not yet support a structurally re-rated specialty compounder.

summary.one_line: OCCL is a low-leverage, qualified insoluble-sulphur incumbent with idle capacity and a tightening Indian trade-remedy option. Its FY26 profit was acid-led, tax-assisted and absorbed by working capital, and the Rs 219 price sits far above every scenario in our DCF while resting on a single unexplained 28%-margin quarter.
